title: The Impossible Road to Rome
hook: Part 2. What happens when a treaty line becomes the fuse for another war?
full_narration: Part 2. What happens when a treaty line becomes the fuse for another war? In 226 BCE, the Ebro Treaty cuts Iberia into warning signs. [[pause:0.4]] Hasdrubal's diplomacy holds the line, until his death opens command. In 221 BCE, adult Hannibal Barca takes the army in Iberia. [[voice:tense]] The old oath now has cavalry, silver, and waiting soldiers. In 219 BCE, Saguntum falls after Hannibal's hard siege. [[pause:0.6]] Rome sees a Roman-tied city broken, and the Senate demands war. In 218 BCE, Carthage and Rome enter the Second Punic War. Hannibal refuses the expected road, and turns north into Gaul. [[voice:low]] He crosses the Pyrenees, the Rhône, then the merciless Alps. Rome never expected him in Italy; Ticinus proves he is real. At Trebbia, Rome breaks again, and central Italy waits in dread. [[pause:0.8]] Follow for part 3.

youtube_description: Part 2 of The Fall of Carthage follows the spark that turns a treaty line into open war. In Iberia, the Ebro Treaty draws a fragile boundary between Rome and Carthage. Then Hannibal Barca takes command, and Saguntum becomes the crisis point. By 218 BCE, the Second Punic War begins. But Hannibal does not take the road Rome expects. He drives his army through Gaul, across the Pyrenees, the Rhône, and the Alps, then appears in northern Italy like a nightmare. At Ticinus and Trebbia, Rome learns the war has come home.
